Member: Emerson Delgado, Member ID W727121486
Requested Service: Lumbar fusion, CPT 22612
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-07
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-03

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for lumbar (lower back) fusion, CPT 22612, as set forth in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-07. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I am submitting this letter, together with the attached clinical records from my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, MD (orthopedic surgery), to demonstrate that the medical-necessity criteria in Regence's own governing medical policy have in fact been met and documented.

**Policy at issue.** Regence's Medical Policy Manual, Surgery, Policy No. SUR187, "Lumbar Spinal Fusion" (the version publicly available at the time of this appeal reflects an effective date of July 1, 2026, with last review March 2026), lists CPT 22612 among the codes governed by this policy and sets out the medical-necessity criteria for lumbar fusion. I ask that Regence confirm which specific version of SUR187 was applied to my request and, if it differs from the version cited here, provide me a copy of that version, as I am relying on the publicly posted policy text.

The policy states that documentation is required to support the criteria: "Clinical documentation to support criteria is required (See Required Documentation)." My clinical record satisfies this requirement, and the enclosed records identify exactly where.

**Applicable criterion: Spinal stenosis, Section I.C.**

SUR187 provides that lumbar spinal fusion "may be considered medically necessary" where the individual has:

"C. Spinal stenosis when all of the following Criteria are met: 1. Neurogenic claudication or radicular pain; and 2. Documented central, lateral recess, or foraminal stenosis, with or without disc protrusion/herniation, facet arthropathy or facet cyst, or ligamentum flavum hypertrophy on MRI or other advanced imaging consistent with the individual's symptoms; and 3. Spondylolisthesis at a level (L1-S1) to be included in the fusion demonstrated on x-rays, CT, or MRI or there is a high likelihood of post-operative instability due to severity of stenosis and extent of decompression/facetectomy as evidenced with findings including but not limited to disruption of the posterior elements due to facet joint excision that exceeds 50% bilaterally or 75% or more of a single facet during spinal decompression, removal of the pars interarticularis that requires fusion to stabilize, or complete or partial corpectomy; and 4. There is either clinical documentation of significant functional impairment or disability, or objective measurement of severe disability using the Oswestry Disability Index tool; and 5. There is clinical documentation that a minimum of three months of conservative nonoperative therapy failed to adequately treat the individual's current symptoms including one or more of the following: a. Documented cauda equina syndrome, progressive motor loss, or subjective worsening of symptoms during a course of conservative management when clearly documented in the medical record; or b. All of the following Criteria are met: i. Physical therapy or professionally-directed therapeutic independent home exercise program unless contraindication is clearly documented; and ii. Two or more of the following treatment modalities have been attempted: a.) Prescription anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics, or prescription strength doses of OTC anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics; or b.) Adjunctive medications such as nerve membrane stabilizers or muscle relaxants; or c.) Alternative therapies such as, but not limited to acupuncture, chiropractic manipulation, massage therapy, yoga, meditation; or d.) Injection therapy of epidural or facet joint implicated pain sources in the area of concern, including but not limited to epidural steroid injection, medial branch block, radiofrequency ablation, selective nerve root injection, or discogram; and 6. The individual is nicotine-free OR there is clinical documentation that the individual has been abstinent from nicotine use for at least six weeks prior to planned procedure based on attestation or laboratory results (cotinine or nicotine levels); or"

**Application of the record to each element of Criterion I.C.:**

1. *Neurogenic claudication or radicular pain.* The physical examination documents neurogenic claudication with diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes, and I cannot stand or walk more than 10 minutes before leg pain and heaviness force me to stop, relieved by sitting — the classic pattern of neurogenic claudication.

2. *Documented central, lateral recess, or foraminal stenosis on MRI or other advanced imaging consistent with the individual's symptoms.* The MRI of the lumbar spine dated 2026-05-29 documents severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina, directly consistent with my claudication and radicular symptoms.

3. *Spondylolisthesis at a level (L1-S1) to be included in the fusion demonstrated on imaging.* The same imaging workup, including flexion-extension radiographs dated 2026-05-29, documents grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5 with 5 mm of translation on flexion-extension — the level proposed for fusion.

4. *Clinical documentation of significant functional impairment or disability.* My record documents that I cannot stand or walk more than 10 minutes before leg pain and heaviness force me to stop. [If a formal Oswestry Disability Index score was calculated, please insert it here; the enclosed records document functional impairment in narrative form, which the policy accepts as an alternative to an ODI score under the "either/or" language quoted above.]

5. *Minimum of three months of conservative nonoperative therapy that failed, including required modalities.* My record documents 14 months of progressive symptoms and reflects (b)(i) supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, over 10 weeks (2026-05-07 to 2026-07-16, 16 visits, per the physical therapy discharge note), and (b)(ii) at least two of the listed treatment modalities: (a) NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief, and (d) a corticosteroid (epidural/facet-area) injection on 2026-05-18 that provided only 4 weeks of partial relief. This satisfies both the duration requirement and the "two or more" modality requirement in subsection 5.b.

6. *Nicotine status.* I am a non-smoker, satisfying the requirement that "the individual is nicotine-free."

In addition, my record documents no active infection, no untreated substance use, and a BMI of 29, none of which are disqualifying factors under the quoted criteria.

**Response to the stated denial reason.** The denial states only that the submitted documentation was "incomplete" and did not permit a determination of medical necessity, without specifying which element(s) of the applicable criteria were considered unmet or absent. As shown above, the record already contains documentation addressing every enumerated element of Section I.C: symptom type, imaging findings, level-specific instability, functional impairment, a three-month-plus trial of at least two conservative modalities plus supervised physical therapy, and nicotine status. I therefore ask that Regence identify, in writing, the specific element(s) of Section I.C. (or any other applicable criterion in SUR187) that the reviewer found unsupported, so that any genuine documentation gap can be promptly corrected. If the missing item is solely a formal Oswestry Disability Index score, I ask that Regence confirm whether the narrative functional-impairment documentation already provided satisfies the "either/or" standard in subsection 4, and if not, I will arrange for my surgeon's office to submit a supplemental ODI assessment.

**Enclosures submitted with this appeal:**
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-07 to 2026-07-16, 16 visits)
- Medication and injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection dated 2026-05-18)
- MRI lumbar spine report, 2026-05-29
- Flexion-extension lumbar radiograph report, 2026-05-29
- Clinical examination notes documenting neurogenic claudication, L5 dermatomal sensory changes, and absence of bowel/bladder dysfunction
- Surgeon's (Dr. Reyes) letter of medical necessity
- [Any Oswestry Disability Index score or other functional assessment, if available]

I understand that this appeal must be received by the deadline stated in the denial notice, 2027-02-03 (180 days from the notice date of 2026-08-07). I am submitting this appeal well in advance of that deadline and request an expedited review given the ongoing neurogenic claudication and progressive nature of my symptoms.

Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to me at the address, phone number, and email listed above, with a copy to Dr. Reyes at [surgeon's office address/fax]. Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the expected timeframe for a determination.

Note on this letter: Only the passages above set off in quotation marks and attributed to SUR187 are text I retrieved directly from Regence's published medical policy document. All other statements are my own description of my clinical record and argument, and I have not quoted or attributed any other language to the plan.

Sincerely,

Emerson Delgado
